Six of the observed peaks in the Raman spectrum of pure zircon (Fig. 2a) were theoretically assigned by Dawson et al. (1971) according to a full crystal-field analysis of the silicate tetrahedra in a crystalline structure with a Dah point-group symmetry (Table 2) The four highest frequency modes are internal stretching and bending vibrations of the (SiO,)4 tetrahedra; whereas, the modes at 224 and 201 Acm are lattice modes: The intensity of the bands with the Eg symmetry (see Table 2) depends on the orientation of the zircon crystal with respect to the polarization plane of the exciting laser light.
